title.en: Understanding the bridge from childhood to adulthood

text.en: Between ages 10 and 19, teenagers experience rapid changes in height, voice, emotions, and independence. Knowing what is normal helps you stay confident, healthy, and informed.

Adolescence (ages 10 to 19) is the crucial transition from childhood to adulthood, marked by rapid physical, mental, emotional, and social changes.
Puberty activates growth and sex hormones, causing a growth spurt, body hair growth, active sweat and oil glands, voice change in boys, and menstruation in girls.
Every adolescent develops at a unique pace—comparing yourself to others is unhelpful, and wet dreams in boys or menstruation in girls are completely natural.
Personal and menstrual hygiene (clean sanitary pads, safe disposal in bins/pits/incinerators, washing hands) protects health; CWSN (Children With Special Needs) should also be supported.
Early or teenage pregnancy carries serious health risks for both mother and fetus because full reproductive and physical maturity is not yet reached.
Body Mass Index (BMI = weight in kg / height in m²) checks healthy weight (normal range 18–25; overweight >25 to <29; obese >30). Chapter 3 also introduces pharmacology (therapeutic vs unwanted drug effects).
Adolescence spans ages 10 to 19 and brings rapid physical, emotional, and social growth.
Hormones trigger puberty changes at different rates for each person—everyone's pace is unique.
Menstruation and wet dreams are normal physiological processes, never a cause for shame.
Proper menstrual hygiene includes clean pads and safe disposal in bins or incinerators.
Adolescent pregnancy risks the health of both the young mother and the developing fetus.
Calculate BMI as weight (kg) divided by height squared (m²); normal BMI is 18 to 25.

problem.en: A student weighs 50 kg and is 1.60 m tall. Calculate their BMI and classify it.

why.en: BMI formula divides weight by height squared.

text.en: Divide weight by height²: 50 / 2.56 ≈ 19.5, which is within the normal range (18–25).

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking everyone must grow at the exact same age or that wet dreams/menstruation are abnormal

points.en: Adolescence (10–19 years) involves rapid physical, mental, emotional, and social development.
Puberty changes occur at individual rates; wet dreams and menstruation are normal.
Personal and menstrual hygiene and avoiding teenage pregnancy are vital for health.
BMI = weight (kg) / height (m²); normal range is 18 to 25.
